title: Aspirate a tilted flask with the tip at its back wall
instruction: Aspirate the spent medium out of the open flask with the aspirator without touching the cell layer, then lay the flask flat on its outline, put the aspirator back on its stand and let go.
context: Why: adherent cells grow as a layer on a culture flask's floor, and their medium is changed every two to three days and before every passage, inside a Class II biological safety cabinet: the old medium is drawn off with a vacuum aspirator, one hand tilting the flask while the other aspirates. Protocols say to keep the tip in the medium and to touch the bottom only at the very end, at the low wall. The knack: tilted neck-up and onto one side, the medium runs to the low back corner, and the pipette goes about 13 cm through the neck to rest at the back wall while the other hand keeps the flask still. Aspirated flat, about 2 mL stays behind; a tip on the floor scrapes the cells off. Robots do this inside Class II cabinets built for automation (NuAire custom robotic BSCs; Erlab H.Box hoods for robots), keeping the cabinet's rules: work at least 4 in inside the front grille, grilles clear. Done by: research technicians and students in any cell-culture lab, several times a week per flask.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), heights above the work surface. Cabinet: the two-arm robot works inside a Thermo Scientific 1300 Series Class II Type A2 biological safety cabinet, 4-foot, interior 1199 x 780 x 630 mm (W x H x D; maker's brochure), stainless steel; arm bases 15 cm behind the 10 cm front air grille, the sash behind them at its 10 in (254 mm) working height, the back wall at x 48.0 cm with a 5 cm rear exhaust grille, the HEPA diffuser 78 cm up. What binds: the right elbow passes 4.4 cm from the right wall, the left 4-5 cm from the back wall (a 3-foot cabinet is too narrow); an arm link past a wall, the ceiling or the sash plane scores 0; the 4 in line and rear grille stay clear. Repeated trials may use a full-size plywood mock of this interior (acrylic sash, tape-band grilles). Culture flask: SPL Life Sciences 70075 T75 tissue-culture flask, polystyrene, 1.5 mm walls, body 124.1 x 84.2 x 39.6 mm, growth area 75 cm2, a short neck 21.5 mm bore and 22 mm long centred on its end face, 60 g empty, cap off and set aside. It lies flat on its outline, growth face down, long axis along y, the neck toward the robot's right (-y), its back wall's outer face at y 10.0 cm and its centre line at x 29.0 cm; free. It holds 15.0 mL of water dyed red (the medium, about 2 mm deep over the floor). A marker line on the outside of the floor runs 10 mm from the back wall; the floor beyond it (the cell layer) carries a witness layer: 7.5 mL of 1% agarose (microwaved to clear, cooled to 55 C) dyed blue, poured through the neck onto the flat floor, set in about 5 min (about 1 mm), then scraped off the 10 mm strip; a pipette touch grooves it. Blue painter's tape, 12 mm wide, outlines the flask 4 mm outside its footprint. Aspirator: an INTEGRA VACUBOY hand operator 155510 (plastic hand piece 25 mm across and 130 mm long) with rubber adapter 155505 holding a Fisherbrand 2 mL polystyrene aspirating pipette (275 mm long, 6.18 mm across), 65 g in all, on silicone tubing clipped overhead to a trap. Low-cost route: a PLA tube 25 mm across and 130 mm long as the hand piece, the pipette in silicone tubing to a 500 mL filter-flask trap on an SP Bel-Art water-jet aspirator on a lab tap (about US$42), the rate set with a screw pinch clamp. Suction runs all the time, set so 15 mL is drawn in 7.5 s (2.0 mL/s). Stand: a 3D-printed PLA cradle (a channel under the hand piece, a channel under the pipette, a stop under the hand piece's front face) on columns over a 6 mm steel base plate, 2.0 kg in all, standing on the table to the flask's right. The aspirator rests in it, free, the pipette pointing +y and 35 deg below horizontal, its open tip 270 mm in front of the grip point (10 mm behind the hand piece's front face), the grip point at x 20.0 cm, y -18.0 cm, 22.0 cm up. Friction 0.5 (set). Both arms start in their ready pose. One fixed layout, zero object jitter. Nothing else is on the work surface.
scoring: Judged at the end of the run with a 0.01 g balance, a ruler, a light box and the trial video (a bench-level camera along the flask's floor, and the left wrist camera). Medium left: the flask's mass minus its written empty mass, 1 g = 1 mL (sim: the volume rule's medium left, film included). Cell layer touched: at any time, the pipette on the 1 mm witness layer (1.02 mm above the floor: within 0.02 mm of its top) more than 10 mm from the back wall (real: first, a bench-level camera frame of the tip on the layer beyond the marker line; second, any groove there on the light box). Flat on its outline: the floor within 5 deg of level and every footprint corner within 20 mm of its taped place. On its stand: the hand piece resting in both channels, within 5 mm and 5 deg of its starting rest. Released and still: no gripper within 20 mm of the flask or the aspirator, and neither moving more than 1 mm over the last 2 s. Score 0 if, at any time, even if put right after: liquid leaves the flask other than up the pipette (sim: the surface reaches the mouth's lowest lip; real: a red spot on the pad or bench), or the flask or the aspirator is dropped (falls more than 20 mm within 0.25 s), or a cabinet rule is broken: the flask, aspirator or stand within 4 in (102 mm) of the front grille or resting on the rear grille, or any part of either arm outside the cabinet's interior (past the sash's plane, the back or side walls or the ceiling; real: the trial video and tape lines on the work surface). Otherwise, at the end, the first that fits: 1.0 if 0.50 mL or less is left, the flask is flat on its outline, the aspirator is on its stand, both are released and still for 2 s and the cell layer was never touched; 0.75 if 1.0 mL or less is left with the flask flat on its outline, the aspirator on its stand and both released and still, or 0.50 mL or less is left without that; 0.5 if 3.0 mL or less is left; 0.25 if 10.0 mL or less is left, and at most 0.25 whenever the cell layer was touched; 0 if more than 10.0 mL is left, including the untouched start. Removed medium never comes back; a flask tilted again or an aspirator picked up again loses the put-back credit. Which corner, which hand does what, how the flask is held and in what order things are put back are not scored. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The trial ends at the run limit; only the end counts.
run_limit: 3,600 steps (3 minutes at 20 Hz); the scripted two-arm demo takes about 73 s (1,457 steps)
reset_notes: Empty the trap bottle if it is over half full. Pour any liquid left in the flask into the waste, shake out the drops and dry the outside; check the witness layer on the light box (re-pour it if grooved). Once per session, rest the aspirator's tip for 1 s on a spare prepared flask's layer (the aspirator's own 65 g): a groove must show on the light box, else pour 0.5% agarose. Before every trial, stand the flask on its end, aspirate its corner dry, weigh it with its layer and write that empty mass (the gel loses water), then refill 15.0 mL of dyed water with a 25 mL serological pipette and check 15.0 g over it. Lay the flask flat on its taped outline, cap off. Reseat the pipette 15 mm in the adapter, check the suction runs, and lay the hand piece in both channels of the stand against the stop. Replace the underpad if it has any spot. Nothing is used up but water. Once a day, time 15 mL into a cylinder: 7.5 s (2.0 mL/s), set with the residual-suction screw or the pinch clamp. Run the simulator with -E object_jitter=0 (one fixed layout).
fidelity: Rigid parts; no tubing. Cabinet: work surface, walls, grilles, sash frame drawn; sash glass, ceiling: scorer limits. Medium: a volume rule, a level surface over what is left in the flask's real interior, plus a film (0.25 mm on a level floor, 0.02 mm once it slopes 20 deg). A tip below the surface draws 2.0 mL/s down to its rim; a full lip spills. Witness gel: a 1 mm layer, touched at 0.02 mm. Floor and back-wall colliders 6 mm thick, outward (flask 4.5 mm higher). Static = dynamic friction.
